chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Sadīr, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): “I left those devoted to your wilayah differing, some of them disavowing others.”

He said: “And what have you to do with that? The people have only been charged with three things: recognizing the Imams, submitting to them in what comes to them, and referring back to them in that wherein they differ.”

key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams as the divinely designated authorities
key_terms.مَوَالِيَكَ: those devoted to your wilayah and allegiance

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام say believers must do when they differ?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the central duty of the believers is not to become absorbed in mutual estrangement, but to know the Imams, submit to their authority, and return disputed matters to them. It emphasizes the Imam’s role as the decisive religious authority and presents unity through recognition and submission to Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
